cohort: 114 singleton pregnancies with idiopathic polyhydramnios compared to 114 normal pregnancies
finding: Pregnancies complicated by idiopathic polyhydramnios had higher rates of adverse perinatal outcomes, including low birth weight, NICU admission, fetal distress, fetal death, lower APGAR scores, preterm delivery, and neonatal death.
birth_weight: Low birth weight (<2500 g), macrosomia (>4000 g)
